messages:
Anya K.: heads-up — starting an async thread for the hotpath stabilization sprint. goal: land kernel perf patch + continuous batching improvements + KV warmup heuristics by end of week. quick ownership propose: Michael (kernel), Sophia (batching), Jamal (KV). blockers: allocator bump from eng-infra, and a perf regression seen in canary.
Michael T.: ack. I can own kernel. I listed the open PRs in my queue — will triage. which perf regression are we tracking?
Anya K.: the canary from this morning shows 8–12% p50 increase for short sequences (<=128). link to logs: https://redwood.example/canary/17234 — summarized in the thread below.
Sophia L.: assigning batching owner. I'm worried about batching latency tail when batch sizes spike. need to confirm continuous batching backpressure logic. can we add a short perf test that simulates spikes?
Jamal R.: KV warmup: I have a prototype for prefix caching + prefetch TTL. Current concern: prefetch handshake sometimes thrashes when coldstarts overlap. I'll add a guard to only prefetch when active_connections > 1.
Dinesh P.: eng-infra here — allocator rollout (jemu-alloc v2) is scheduled tomorrow at 09:00 PT in staging; production later in the week. Michael, that allocator changes allocation alignment; might affect kernel memory layout. plan to coordinate.
Michael T.: thanks @Dinesh P. — can you post the staging CI job link? I want to run our microbench against it.
Dinesh P.: https://ci.redwood.example/job/alloc-v2-staging — note: feature flag alloc_v2 = true in staging.
Sophia L.: here's a quick perf script I used locally:
```
# run perf harness
./bin/run_perf --model gpt-small --seq 128 --concurrency 40 --duration 60
```
sample output: p50=18ms, p95=78ms, /tokens=0.85k/s
Sophia L.: I'll add a job that runs that against staging allocator + current batching changes.
runtime-bot: canary-report: canary-17234 — 2026-03-16 08:12 UTC — p50 +9%, p95 +15%, error rate 0.2%. (tags: allocator-change, batching-experiment)
Jamal R.: quick question — if we gate prefetch behind active_connections, does that hurt throughput for low-concurrency tenants? maybe parameterize by tenant_tier or warmup_budget. thoughts?
Anya K.: good catch. Jamal, parameterize with a per-tenant budget and fall back to synchronous warmup if budget exhausted. add config: `kv.prefetch_budget` (default 1).
Michael T.: action items: 1) I will open a tracker issue for allocator integration + kernel memory tests (PR by EOD). 2) run microbench against alloc-v2 staging job and report numbers.
Sophia L.: action items: 1) add spike perf job to CI and run against staging; 2) add a small canary that exercises continuous batching with variable arrival rates.
Jamal R.: action items: 1) land prefetch guard + budget flag; 2) add unit test for overlapping coldstarts.
Anya K.: timeline: pair sync at 15:00 PT today (kernel + batching + KV owners). please update the tracker with your PR/issue links before then. if alloc-v2 causes regressions, fallback plan is to pin allocator via feature flag per node group.
Michael T.: noted. I'll post PR link: https://phabricator.redwood/PR/5421 when ready. :thumbsup:
Sophia L.: I'll create the CI job and share link.
Jamal R.: PR will be up in ~2h.
Anya K.: thanks everyone. if anything blocks the pairing, ping here. otherwise we'll run the pairing and report outcomes in this same thread. :wave:
